newsitem.title: FRANCE: French vote may make meeting Maastricht harder.
newsitem.headline: French vote may make meeting Maastricht harder.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac told German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Friday the French election campaign had raised expectations which could make it harder to meet Maastricht treaty criteria on a single currency, a French source said.

"The president presented the new situation in France, where things were said in the campaign and expectations were created that may be an additional complicating factor in achieving the criteria," the source said.

Chirac asked Kohl to show understanding for the new French position on the European Union's "stability pact" limiting budget deficits, given both countries' attachment to achieving Economic and Monetary Union.

"The president underlined that Europe suffered from a perception...of being too monetarist and technocratic and a way must be found to take account of citizens' concerns, especially about employment," the source said.
The French source said Kohl had replied that no one was willing to abandon the stability pact which was absolutely necessary to achieve monetary union.
"Each (country) is determined to hold to the criteria and that presupposes efforts. Kohl said that and so did the president," the source said.

The source said there were several proposals for a resolution meeting France's concern to coordinate economic policies better to promote growth and jobs. "We think there will be an agreement in Amsterdam," the source said.
